answer.memory_text: mem_031 · Experiment #103 — site-wide 40% launch discount, SMB traffic (day 21→51): signup +31% · qualified leads +2% · 30-day retention -12%. Lesson: price discounting bought raw signups that did not convert to qualified pipeline and broke the retention guardrail (-12% vs -3% limit); the acquired cohort churns before first renewal. Treat headline signup lift from discounting as a vanity metric. Rolled back day 51. Scope: measured on SMB only; NOT tested on enterprise or developer — do not assume the magnitude transfers, but treat discount-led acquisition as guardrail-risky until proven otherwise. Confidence: high on the negative result (full 30-day window); mechanism (self-selected bargain seekers vs. mix shift) unverified.
missing_evidence: Whether the retention drop is driven by a low-intent discount cohort or by mix shift within SMB (cohort-level retention split by discount vs. non-discount signups)
Post-rollback retention recovery for the day 21–51 cohort at 60/90 days
Whether any of the +31% signups eventually convert to qualified enterprise-grade accounts on a longer lag
Revenue impact net of discount, not just signup/lead counts
answer.next_action: Roll back the 40% discount immediately (retention guardrail breached) and run a cohort-level retention decomposition on the day 21–51 SMB signups; then return focus to the enterprise intent-friction thread from mem_017 with a qualification-gated demo variant.

answer.memory_text: mem_031 · Experiment #103 — site-wide 40% launch discount, measured on SMB traffic, day 21→51: signup +31%, qualified leads +2%, 30-day retention NOT REPORTED (cohort not yet matured; guardrail unverified). Interpretation: signup lift is almost entirely unqualified volume — qualified leads flat, so this is close to the 'volume over quality' pattern the guardrails forbid. No evidence of any effect on enterprise pipeline (primary objective), and the discount was served site-wide while only SMB was analyzed, so enterprise/developer exposure is an unmeasured confound (discount anchoring may depress enterprise ACV). Do NOT treat this as a validated win or extend discounting to enterprise without retention, revenue-per-account, and enterprise-contamination data. Scope: SMB only, provisional. Confidence: low.
missing_evidence: 30-day retention for the discount cohort (guardrail metric, entirely absent)
Revenue per account / ACV and net revenue impact, not just signup counts
Qualified-lead rate per signup (flat absolute leads on +31% signups implies a materially lower conversion rate)
Whether enterprise and developer traffic saw the site-wide discount, and any effect on enterprise ACV, discounting expectations, or pipeline
Churn/refund behavior once the promotional price expires
answer.next_action: Hold the discount as unproven and let the cohort mature to collect 30-day retention, per-signup qualified-lead rate, and revenue per account; simultaneously audit whether enterprise traffic was exposed to the site-wide discount and what it did to enterprise ACV.
